title: Count profiles as sums of linear thresholds
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $a:\mathbb{N}\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. For $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, count the coordinates $i\in S$ with $x_i=1$. If $f(x)$ equals $a$ applied to this count for every $x$, then the real-valued version of $f$ is a constant plus a sum of $2n$ linear threshold functions on the cube.
hypotheses_covered: Subset S of the n coordinates
Function a from natural numbers to signs
Boolean function f on the n-dimensional sign cube
f is determined by a applied to the number of positive coordinates in S
